parsed.why: No trans-specific offence and court-recognised third-gender tradition, but implementation gaps, documented public harassment of visibly trans people, conversion therapy and rising political hostility; worst feature is societal hostility with thin recourse.

No criminalisation of identity or expression; convictions upheld for assaulting trans tourists and an officer jailed for beating a trans woman, so recourse works. Residual societal hostility, northern anti-trans sentiment and custody gaps cap it.

Enforced sodomy code, de facto ban on being trans, raids and convictions using 'gay appearance' as evidence, police complicity in beatings, torture and vigilante killings with impunity, no advocacy or recourse.

No express offence, but morality provisions are used against people and conduct is de facto illegal; no recognition or discrimination law, pervasive taboo, extremely thin documentation and no protective infrastructure. Extrapolated toward risk, not midpoint.

Unenforced 10-year sodomy statute plus a public-order offence targeting deception as to one's sex — reaching visible presentation; no recognition, rising fundamentalist hostility, activist murdered. Indigenous third-gender acceptance partially offsets.
